sentences.text: This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 04-03-2024 at about 7.15 a.m., the petitioner was riding the scooter bearing No.KA-04-JE-2665 on 6th main road of Nagapura ward, from Geleyara Bhalaga towards 11th cross, very carefully, cautiously, by observing traffic rules and regulations.

When he was near Sanjeevini Medicals, at that time all of a sudden one school bus bearing No.KA-51-B-0737, driven by its driver with high speed, in rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life, came from the opposite direction of Shankarmath road and dashed against the scooter of the petitioner.
Due to said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, she was shifted to Prestine Hospital, Bengaluru,
wherein she took treatment as an in-patient.
Earlier to the accident she was working as a Technician at Diagnostic Centre and earning a sum of Rs.50,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, she has become permanently disabled and thereby lost her earning capacity.
The Rajajinagar Traffic Police have registered the case against the driver of the said bus for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 338 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondent No.1 has appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement.
Whereas, the respondent No.2 did not choose to appear and remained absent.
Hence, the respondent No.2 is placed as ex-parte.
4. The respondent No.1 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.

It has admitted the issuance of passenger carrying commercial vehicle insurance policy vide No.D106585130/23062023, valid from 23-02-2024 to 23-02-2023 in respect of Tata passenger carrying vehicle bearing No.KA-51-B-0737, in favour of the respondent No.2.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
It has denied the occurrence and mode of the alleged accident and also actionable negligence of the driver of the school bus bearing No.KA-51-B-0737.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries, medical expenses and treatment taken by her.
It has contended that, the petition is bad for non-compliance of provision under Sections 134(c) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.

It has denied that, the alleged Molly Alexander vs Go Digit General Insurance Limited on 1 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25194918/
2 accident is caused by the driver of the insured school bus, but the petitioner herself was negligent and has caused the alleged accident.

sentences.text: The petitioner is not entitled to seek for any compensation from the respondents, for her own negligent act in causing the accident.

Further it is contended that, the petitioner being the rider of the scooter bearing No.KA-04-JE-2665 was not holding valid and effective driving licence to ride the scooter and she was not wearing safety helmet while riding the scooter and she has violated traffic rules.
Further it is contended that, the driver of the insured school bus bearing No.KA-51-B-0737 was also not holding valid driving licence to drive that class of motor vehicle.
The respondent No.2 knowingly and intentionally entrusted the school bus to a person who had no valid driving licence to drive the school bus.
Therefore, he has contravened the proviso of the Motor Vehicles Act and the Rules framed there under and has committed the breach of the terms and conditions of the policy.
Hence, this respondent is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner.
Further it is contended that, the bus bearing No.KA-51-B-0737 was not having valid permit to ply at the place of accident, as on the date of accident.
Further it is contended that, the charge-sheeted driver of the insured school bus has been falsely implanted by suppressing the material facts.
by colluding with the jurisdictional police and the owner of the said bus to obtain compensation from the insurance company fraudulently.
Further, it has sought for permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.2, as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, she has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident, alleged to have occurred on 04-03-2024 at about 7.15 a.m., infront of Sanjeevini Medical, 115h Cross, Nagapura main road, Mahalakshmi Layout,
Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the School Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-51-B-0737 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3. What order or Award ?
6.

Further, she has got examined one more witness namely Dr. S.A.
Somashekhara as P.W.2.

On the other hand, the respondent No.1 has examined the Superintendent of RTO, Electronic City and its representative/Associate Legal Claims Manager as R.W.1 and R.W.2 respectively and got marked total 10 documents as Ex.R.1 to 10.
7.
I have heard the arguments of both the sides and perused the entire material placed on record.

In support of his arguments, the learned counsel for respondent No.1 has relied on the following decisions:

Due to said impact, the petitioner has fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Further it is contended that, earlier to the accident she was working as Technician at Diagnostic Centre and earning a sum of Rs.50,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, she has become permanently disabled and thereby lost her earning capacity.
10. In order to prove her case, the petitioner has got examined herself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein she has reiterated the entire averments made in the petition.
Further, in support of her oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked total 16 documents as Ex.P.1 to 16.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is true copy of F.I.R., Ex.P.2 is true copy of first information statement, Ex.P.3 is true copy of sketch, Ex.P.4 is true copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P.5 is true copy of notice under Section 133 of Motor Vehicles Act, Ex.P.6 is true copy of reply to notice under Section 133 of Motor Vehicles Act, Ex.P.7 is true copy of wound certificate,

At the outset, is it pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
involvement of school bus bearing Reg. No.KA-51-B-0737 in the said accident, the issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.1 in respect of said vehicle and its validity as on the date of accident, are not in dispute.

Further, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner has remained undisputed by the owner of offending vehicle/Respondents No.2, as he did not choose file his written statement and contest the case of the petitioner.

Whereas, the respondent No.1 has specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and taken specific defence that, the alleged accident has taken place solely due to rash and negligent riding of motorcycle by the petitioner and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of offending school bus.
But, the respondent No.1 has failed to establish the said contentions.

Except the self serving statements of R.W.2, who is the representative/Associate Legal Claims Manager of respondent No.1 insurance company, there is no other corroborative oral or documentary evidence placed on record by the respondents to show that, the said accident has taken place solely due to rash and negligent riding of scooter by the petitioner herself and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of offending school bus.
If really the said accident has taken place due to the negligence of the petitioner herself, the same could have been easily established by examining the eye-witness to the alleged accident.
But, the respondent No.1 has not taken any strain to examine the independent eye-witness to the said accident, for the reasons best known to it.

In such circumstances, there is absolutely no independent corroborative evidence on record to show that, at the relevant point of time of accident the petitioner was riding her scooter in rash and negligent manner and the accident took place due to her own negligence.

On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending school bus bearing Reg.
No.KA-51-B-0737 and dashing the same to the scooter of the petitioner from behind and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries on both the hands.

Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.1 has cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence or which goes to show that, the said accident has taken place solely due to rash and negligent riding of the scooter by the petitioner or there was any contributory negligence on her part in the cause of accident.

13. Further, the Ex.P.3 sketch and Ex.P.4 spot mahazar also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place infront of Sanjeevini Medical, 11th Cross, Nagapura main road, Mahalakshmi Layout,
Bengaluru, in between the offending school bus bearing Reg. No.KA-51-B-0737 and on coming scooter bearing No.KA-04-JE-2665 of the petitioner, which was proceeding from Geleyarabalaga towards 11th cross.

Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.8,
the accident has not taken place due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

When the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of the petitioner, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle.
On the other hand, the respondent No.1 has not produced any rebuttal evidence to show that, the said documents are false and concocted documents.

Further, the investigation officer in his Ex.P.9 final report/charge- sheet has clearly stated that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending school bus bearing Reg. No.KA-51-B-0737 and the petitioner has sustained grievous Molly Alexander vs Go Digit General Insurance Limited on 1 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25194918/
5 injuries in the said accident.

sentences.text: Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged either by the driver or the owner of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-51-B-0737.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident, negligence of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

14. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.7 wound certificate, Ex.P.10 discharge summary, Ex.P.15 OPD book along with clinical notes and Ex.P.16 x-rays (total 3), it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident.
She has suffered right hand displaced fracture 2nd metacarpal and left wrist displaced distal radius collar's fracture.

The P.W.2, who is the doctor who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability, has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the petitioner has sustained above injuries in the road traffic accident.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.1 has cross-examined P.W.2 in length, nothing worth has been brought out from his mouth, which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
On the other hand, there is no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondent No.1 to show that, the above medical records produced by the petitioner are false documents.

15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, " in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."

17. Therefore, in the light of ratio laid down in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, she has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 04-03-2024 at about 7.15 a.m., infront of Sanjeevini Medical, 11th Cross, Nagapura main road, Mahalakshmi Layout,
Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending school bus bearing Reg.
No.KA-51-B-0737.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.
18. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending school bus bearing Reg. No.KA-51-B-0737 and she has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
As per the medical records placed on record by the petitioner, she has sustained right hand displaced fracture 2nd metacarpal and left wrist displaced distal radius collar's fracture.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary Molly Alexander vs Go Digit General Insurance Limited on 1 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25194918/
6 damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non- pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.

sentences.text:
The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income: In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
To prove her age, the petitioner has produced the notarised copy of her Aadhar card and driving licence, which are marked as Ex.P.13 and 14.
As per Ex.P.13 and 14, the date of birth of the petitioner is 15-08-1967.
The accident has taken place on 04-03-2024 at about 7.15 A.M.
Therefore, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident was 57 years.

Further, the P.W.2, who is the doctor, who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability, has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered right hand displaced fracture 2nd metacarpal and left wrist displaced distal radius collar's fracture and for the said injuries the petitioner has undergone surgeries.

Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries suffered by the petitioner he found that, the petitioner has suffered permanent physical disability of 34% to both upper limbs and 17% to the whole body.

The Ex.P.7 wound certificate, Ex.P.10 discharge summary, Ex.P.15 OPD book along with clinical notes and Ex.P.16 x-rays (total 3) also clearly speaks that, the petitioner has suffered the above stated injuries and for the said injuries she has undergone surgery.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.1 has cross-examined P.W.2 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
He has clearly denied the suggestions made to him that, the petitioner has not suffered any disability and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability.

Further it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.2 has deposed in his evidence that, the accident has occurred on 04-03-2024 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 03-06-2025, which is after lapse of one year and three months from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner.
Further he has admitted that, muscle power around left wrist to the extent of 1 grade is mild loss of muscle power, the fractures are united and implants have been removed.

Therefore, in such circumstances and taking into consideration the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, avocation of the petitioner, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence on record, this Court is of the opinion that,
considering the disability of 10% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 10% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
a) The petitioner has deposed in her evidence that, before accident she was working as Technician at Diagnostic Centre and earning a sum of Rs.50,000/- per month.
Further, she has deposed that, due to the accidental injuries she has become permanently disabled and thereby lost her earning capacity.
The respondent No.1 has specifically denied the same.

In such circumstances, the burden Molly Alexander vs Go Digit General Insurance Limited on 1 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25194918/
7 was on the petitioner to prove her avocation and income.

sentences.text: But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
She has not produced any document to show that, before accident she was working as Technician at Diagnostic Centre and earning a sum of Rs.50,000/- per month.
In such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident has taken place in the year 2024.
Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.16,500/- per month and the annual income of the petitioner as Rs.1,98,000/-.

b) As per the ratio laid down in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the appropriate multiplier for a person whose is aged about 57 years is 9.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, loss of future income is total annual income X disability/100 X multiplier = Rs.1,98,000 X 10/100 X 9 = Rs.1,78,200/-.
ii) Medical expenses:

The petitioner has deposed that, she has incurred expenses of Rs.2,50,000/-
towards medical, conveyance, food & nourishment, attendant charges and other incidental charge.
In order to prove the same, she has produced medical bill, as per Ex.P.11.
The said bill has been examined carefully and found that the petitioner has spent total amount of Rs.1,71,360/- towards medical expenses.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,71,360/- under the head of medical expenses.
iii) Pain and sufferings:

In the present case the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries i.e., right hand displaced fracture 2nd metacarpal and left wrist displaced distal radius collar's fracture and for the said injuries the petitioner has undergone surgery.
As per Ex.P.10 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 8 days, from 04-03-2024 to 11-03-2024, in Pristine Hospital, Bengaluru.
She has also undergone surgery.
Further, as per P.W.2 the said injuries have caused physical disability to the petitioner.
In such circumstances, certainly the petitioner would have suffered pain and sufferings.

Therefore, taking into considering the injuries sustained and the disability suffered by the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, compensation amount of Rs.50,000/- is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.
iv) Attendant charges:
As per Ex.P.10 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 8 days in Pristine Hospital, Bengaluru.
She might have spent some amount towards attendant charges during that period.
Therefore, compensation of Rs.1000 x 8 = Rs.8,000/- is awarded towards the attendant charges.
v) Food and nourishment:
As per Ex.P.10 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 8 days in Pristine Hospital, Bengaluru.
She might have spent some amount for food and nourishment during that period.
Therefore, compensation of Rs. 800 x 8 = Rs.6,400/- is awarded towards food and nourishment charges.
vi) Conveyance expenses:

The petitioner is the resident of No.FF101, Girija Enclave, Thindlu Bus Stop, Vidyaranyapura, Bengaluru North, the accident has taken place infront of Sanjeevini Medical,
11th Cross, Nagapura main road, Mahalakshmi Layout, Bengaluru and she has taken treatment at Pristine Hospital, Bengaluru.

Taking into consideration the distance in between the place of Molly Alexander vs Go Digit General Insurance Limited on 1 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25194918/
8 accident and the above hospitals, compensation of Rs.10,000/- is awarded towards conveyance.

sentences.text: vii) Loss of income during treatment period:
The petitioner has taken treatment for 8 days as in-patient at Pristine Hospital, Bengaluru, for the grievous injuries sustained by her.
She might have taken rest for about 2 months and lost her income for the said period.

Therefore, Rs.16,500 x 2 =
Rs.33,000/- is awarded towards loss of income during treatment period.
viii) Loss of amenities:

It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 57 years and unfortunately she has sustained right hand displaced fracture 2nd metacarpal and left wrist displaced distal radius collar's fracture.
The evidence shows that, she has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 10% to the whole body.
Therefore, awarding compensation of Rs.30,000/- towards loss of amenities would be just and reasonable.
ix) Future medical expenses:
There is no evidence on record to show that, the petitioner requires any further treatment for the injuries sustained in the said accident.
Even, the P.W.2 has not stated anything with respect to same.
The P.W.2 in his cross-examination has admitted that, the fractures are united and implants have been removed.
In such circumstances, the question of awarding future medical expenses does not arise at all.
Therefore, no compensation is awarded in this particular head.

19. Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads as follows :
1. Loss of future income Rs. 1,78,200-00 2.
Medical expenses 1,71,360-00 3. Pain and sufferings 50,000-00
4. Attendant charges 8,000-00 5.
Food and nourishment 6,400-00 6.
Conveyance expenses 10,000-00 7. Loss of income during 33,000-00 treatment period 8. Loss of amenities 30,000-00
9. Future medical expenses Nil
In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,86,960/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of petition till its realization.

sentences.text: Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-51-B- 0737.
As per Ex.R.7 insurance policy bearing No.D106585130/23062023, issued by the respondent No.1, in respect of offending School Bus bearing No.KA-51-B-0737 was valid from 23-06-2023 to 22-06-2024.

As such,
the said policy was valid as on the date of accident i.e. 04-03-2024.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending school bus bearing Reg. No. KA-51- B-0737 the accident in question has occurred and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.2 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.

The respondent No.1 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.2.
21.

But, the learned counsel for respondent No.1 vehemently argued that, as on the date of accident the offending school bus bearing Reg. No.KA-51-B-0737 was not having valid permit to ply the said vehicle at the place of accident.
The Ex.R.8 vehicle particulars extract, Ex.R.9 permit extract and Ex.R.10 vehicle permit history clearly speaks that, as on the date of accident the said vehicle was not having valid permit.

Further argued that, as the insured/respondent No.2 has committed breach of terms and conditions of the insurance policy, the respondent No.1 insurance company is not liable to indemnify the respondent No.2, for any liability or compensation awarded by this Court.
22. On the other hand, the learned counsel for petitioner vehemently argued that, there is no breach of any fundamental terms and conditions of the policy, as alleged by the respondent No.1.

Further argued that, it is settled principle of law that, even if there is a breach of any fundamental condition of the policy, recognised under Sec.149(2) of Motor vehicles Act, the insurance company is liable to pay the compensation to the third party and recover the same from the insured.

23. As rightly argued by the learned counsel for the respondent No.1, as per the Ex.R.8 vehicle particulars extract and Ex.R.9 permit extract, the permit issued by the R.T.O., Electronic City, in respect of offending school bus bearing Reg. No.KA-51-B-0737 was valid from 15-05-2025 to 14-05-2030.

Further, the respondent No.2 being the owner of said vehicle has not produced any document to show that, prior to 15-05-2025 or more particularly as on the date of accident i.e.
04-03-2024 his vehicle was having valid permit to ply at the place of accident.

But, R.W.1, who is the Superintendent of RTO Office, Electronic City, Bengaluru, has clearly admitted in her cross-examination that, as per Ex.R.4 the permit in respect of vehicle bearing No.KA-51-B- 0737 was renewed on 07-09-2017 and usually the permit is issued for the period of 5 years and one can apply for issuance of permit through online process.

Further, mere for the reason that, the offending vehicle was not having permit as on the date accident, the respondent No.1 insurance company cannot be exonerated from its liability to indemnify the insured/respondent No.2, unless it is established that, the offending vehicle was not fit or under good condition to be plied on the public road, as on the date of accident and due to unfit condition of the vehicle the accident has taken place.
In the instant case, there are no such specific allegations in respect of offending vehicle and even nothing with respect to same has been stated in the Ex.P.8 Motor Vehicle Accident report.

15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."
16. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, " in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."
Therefore, in such circumstances and taking into consideration the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, avocation of the petitioner, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence on record, this Court is of the opinion that,
